headline.title: CCL beat its expected move and held it. Up +11.9% at 24.77, through the 24.18 entry on the sheet before the bell and still there twelve minutes in. The rest of the prep needs two corrections. SPY is written as an inside day and is not — Monday's low 763.72 broke Friday's 766.29 and closed under it, which is a 2 Down. And MDB is written as F2D; on the daily it is a clean 2 Down that closed 334.68, far below the 409.18 low it broke.
headline.summary: The distinction on MDB matters because a Failed 2D is a bullish reversal and a 2 Down is not. The bullish case is real but it comes from the intrabar recovery — it traded to 300.00 and closed 334.68, +11.6% off its own low on 17.9M shares against 1.4M Friday — not from the Strat label. The trigger is 344.30, not 344.80: Monday's high was 344.3016, so the sheet's number sits 50 cents above it, which is the safer side to be wrong on. MDB is 326.11 now, −2.6%, and 5.6% below that line. The event is around 10:00 and the sheet says let the market show its hands. It has not yet.

overview:
Monday opened the last week of the quarter on the back foot. S&P −0.8% to 7,684. Two dials did it: the 10-year at 5.24%, another high since 2007, and WTI above $96 intraday.

Both eased overnight. WTI back near $92 on Middle East exports hitting a post-war high. USO −2.8% is the sheet's bullish tell — SPY has not confirmed it, flat at 765.46.

Three names repriced on rules, not sentiment. FICO −19.9%, FHFA folding VantageScore onto the FICO Classic grid. QURE −36.4% on Huntington's data. MDB −18.5% Monday, CEO to Meta.

Today: confidence and JOLTS 9:00 · five Fed speakers. Tomorrow is the one: PCE, ADP, quarter-end, the funding deadline, MU after the close with an analyst day, and investor days at HPE and SNPS.

darkpool.note: For the second straight session Micron owns the board, and it has now been worked from both sides. Monday's largest single-name print ex-ETF was MU $936.1M at the ask, after hours — after Friday's $1.0B at the bid. That is roughly $2B of single-print size through the dark pool in two sessions, on opposite sides, with the report and an analyst day now one sleep away. MU also tops cumulative flow at $5.1B (ask), ahead of NVDA $4.8B (mixed) and META $3.7B (ask). Size like this into a binary event is institutions getting positioned, not a forecast — let Wednesday's price do the talking. The shape of the rest of the list says the same thing: every one of Monday's top ten crossed after hours, and half of it is semis — MU, AVGO, MRVL, NVDA and LRCX all drew size the night before Micron week's main event. The one genuine cross-current is META: $715.6M at the ask on the dark pool while the options board leaned put-side on the same name, taking both the #2 block at $47.3M puts and the #2 sweep. Flow disagreeing with itself on one name is exactly why a side is a lean and not a verdict.
darkpool.right_note: This morning the tape is defensive: ORCL $91.3M on the bid is the biggest print by a wide margin, on its conference day, with CAT $50.0M (bid) and AMGN $50.0M behind it — AMGN tops the six-session flow-leaders list at $291.0M, CAT third at $173.5M. Utilities, insurance-adjacent and infrastructure names catching size the day before PCE. Largest block on the board: WPM $54.5M puts, crossing the session the metals led the down-movers.
